cars.variant: Talladega 428 Cobra Jet automatic — 1969 factory brochure reference
cars.specification_market: 1969 US Ford Talladega road brochure, all four scanned pages visually read. Retains native road-engine figures without inventing a modern net/gross standard. No 427/429 race engine, measured speed, race weight, production quota or road-car victory is inferred. The brochure lists optional Ram-Air, but its actual production availability is not established here and is excluded. Other first-family Torinos, paint, options and renamed variants add no counts.
cars.summary: The Talladega is a road-production icon of the NASCAR aero-war era. Its reshaped nose, grille and bumper were developed for aerodynamic performance rather than cosmetic differentiation. The factory road version paired that body programme with a 428 Cobra Jet and automatic transmission. One original Torino/Fairlane family entry captures this engineering and motorsport connection without assigning race-engine hardware to the street car.

cars.variant: Hurst SC/Rambler 390 four-speed — 1969 factory promotion-sheet reference
cars.specification_market: Original 1969 AMC/Hurst promotion sheet, both sides downloaded and visually read. Native 315 hp carries no invented modern net/gross standard. Advertised quarter-mile claims, tuned 12-second speculation, shipping/curb-weight ambiguity, tyre specifics and prices are not imported. The AMC family album’s early 500-car plan is not final production. A/B paint, Rogue equipment and Group 19 race upgrades do not create extra records or change this stock road reference.
cars.summary: The Hurst SC/Rambler turned AMC’s compact Rogue hardtop into a purpose-built road muscle car. A 390 V8, close-ratio four-speed, Twin-Grip axle, front discs and upgraded chassis equipment made the package substantially more than paint and stripes. Its established Hurst collaboration and drag-oriented road-car concept earn one original Rambler American family entry; colour schemes and dealer racing modifications do not add counts.
